Cost-benefit-risk assessment.title_en: Developing a Statement of Work and Evaluation Criteria (COR407)
Cost-benefit-risk assessment.description_en:
Departments and agencies use a variety of solicitation methods to acquire goods and services through competitive contracts. This course covers two critical elements of the solicitation process: the statement of work and the evaluation criteria for bids submitted. Participants will learn how to write proper requirements to obtain their desired product or service and how to set evaluation criteria that will help select the appropriate bidder.

Topics include:

• identifying the components of a proper statement of work
• understanding the implications of trade agreements
• defining the requirements of the contract
• assessing, managing and mitigating contract risks
• selecting a contractor

Notes:

To gain a better understanding of the subject matter, participants are strongly recommended to complete Overview of Procurement (COR403) or the combination of Procurement Fundamental (COR401) and The Procurement Process (COR402) before registering to COR407.

Decision documentation and traceability.title_en: Framing Opportunities for Effective Data-Driven Decision Making (DDN318)
Decision documentation and traceability.description_en:
Documenting desired business outcomes is a critical part of the decision-making process. This online self-paced course explains how to frame an opportunity by asking the right questions, identifying and testing assumptions, and creating an effective problem statement. Participants will learn about validating assumptions, identifying the opportunity at-hand and ensuring that the proper resources are dedicated to its analysis.

Topics include:

•	making effective data-driven decisions

•	identifying the steps to take to test and validate assumptions

•	asking questions to narrow down a problem

•	defining an initial problem statement •	refining and finalizing problem statements

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support from the International Institute for Analytics.

Departments and agencies use a variety of solicitation methods to acquire goods and services through competitive contracts. This course covers two critical elements of the solicitation process: the statement of work and the evaluation criteria for bids submitted. Participants will learn how to write proper requirements to obtain their desired product or service and how to set evaluation criteria that will help select the appropriate bidder.

• understanding the implications of trade agreements

• assessing, managing and mitigating contract risks
• selecting a contractor

Enterprise and external data ecosystem k.description_en:
Understanding and working with data is essential for making evidence-based decisions in today’s digital workplace. This online self-paced course introduces the importance of data, data-related terminology and the various roles in government which commonly work with data. Through storytelling and interactive learning activities, participants will gain a better understanding of how data, the government and people in Canada are interconnected.

Topics include:

•	defining the data terminology used in the federal public service 

•	identifying the connections between government, data and the public 

•	recognizing the different roles that work with data

Pre-project appraisal and source strateg.description_en:
Project planning in Agile involves establishing the proper project requirements, conditions of satisfaction, and priorities. This online self-paced course examines critical planning activities in Agile such as creating personas and wireframing, as well as iterative methodologies for prioritizing project requirements as part of a release plan. Participants will learn about common Agile estimation techniques such as story points, wideband delphi and affinity estimation.

Topics include:

- defining release planning and iteration planning
- creating personas, user stories and story maps
- understanding the different estimating techniques in Agile
- distinguishing between the different customer-valued prioritization methods
- identifying the key activities of iteration planning meetings

Notes:

This course is part of a Skillsoft learning series that covers the objectives for the PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP)® exam. PMI-ACP is a registered mark of Project Management Institute Incorporated.

Enterprise data holdings and metadata kn.title_en: Information Management: Supporting Programs and Services (COR508)
Enterprise data holdings and metadata kn.description_en:
The proper management of information and data in government organizations is critical to sharing information effectively across departments, with external stakeholders, and with Canadian citizens. This online self-paced course outlines the stages of records and information life-cycle management and reviews information management activities that support programs and services in federal departments. Participants will learn about the different classification systems, advanced search and retrieval techniques and accepted retention and disposition processes.

Topics include:

• managing information resources
• understanding metadata
• developing classification systems
• applying search and retrieval methods
• setting retention specifications

Notes:

It is recommended that learners who are new to the field of information management take Fundamentals of Information Management (I301) before registering for this course.
